title: "Visual SLAM"
description: "A robotics method that estimates a camera's motion while building a map from visual observations."
term: "Visual SLAM"

## Simple explanation

Visual SLAM lets a moving camera work out where it is while simultaneously
building a map of its surroundings from images.

## Technical explanation

Visual simultaneous localization and mapping estimates camera poses and map
structure from a sequence of images. Systems may use feature points or direct
pixel alignment, and may be monocular, stereo, or RGB-D. Estimation often
combines visual measurements with motion models and loop-closure constraints;
monocular systems have scale ambiguity without additional information.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Visual SLAM supports navigation and spatial understanding in robots, AR/VR
devices, and autonomous systems. Reliability depends on camera calibration,
lighting, motion blur, scene texture, dynamic objects, and compute budgets.

## How it works

Detect or track visual features, estimate camera motion between frames, and
triangulate landmarks where geometry permits. A backend optimizes poses and
map points; loop closure recognizes a revisited place and reduces accumulated
drift.

## Practical example

A mobile robot can use stereo camera frames to estimate its trajectory through
a building and map obstacles. The map and pose estimates should be checked
against ground truth or independent sensors before relying on them for
safety-critical navigation.

## Common misconceptions

- SLAM does not produce a perfect global position automatically; estimates can
  drift and may have scale or coordinate-frame ambiguities.
- Visual SLAM is not the same as visual object recognition: it estimates
  geometry and motion, though learned perception may be part of a system.
